brief.goal: Ship an offline mode beta of the field-notes app by the end of Q1, with sync that never loses a note.
brief.audience: The team's engineering and design leads.
brief.assumptions: 4 engineers and 1 designer. The linked repository (example-org/field-notes-app, main) shows how sync works today.
brief.doneWhen: All 7 reviewed sections are approved by the Critic, and anything unresolved is listed under Open questions.

sections.name: Goal
sections.guidance: One or two sentences: the outcome and the deadline.
content: Ship an offline mode beta of the field-notes app by the end of Q1.
Field users can capture and edit notes with no signal, and sync never loses a note.

sections.name: Scope and non-goals
sections.guidance: What is in scope, and explicit non-goals.
content: In scope: create, edit and delete notes offline; queue photo attachments; sync on reconnect.
In scope: a clear offline indicator and a per-note sync status.
Non-goals: tablet layouts, pricing changes, offline search across shared notebooks.
sources: Researcher's answer: field use with no signal

sections.name: Milestones
sections.guidance: 3–5 milestones that each ship user value.
content: 1 · Local storage layer: notes and photos are saved on the device first.
2 · Sync with per-field conflict merge, behind a feature flag.
3 · Offline indicator and sync status in the UI.
4 · Closed beta with [BETA GROUP SIZE] field users.

sections.name: Owners
sections.guidance: Who owns what. Use [PLACEHOLDER] names, never invent people.
content: Overall: [PRODUCT OWNER].
Sync and storage: [ENGINEERING LEAD].
Offline states and messaging: [DESIGNER].
Beta recruitment and feedback: [RESEARCH LEAD].
sources: Section owners from the section plan

sections.name: Timeline
sections.guidance: Phases with rough dates up to the deadline.
content: Weeks 1–3: local storage layer and migration of existing notes.
Weeks 4–7: sync and conflict merge, with a conflict test suite.
Weeks 8–9: offline UI states and internal dogfood.
Weeks 10–12: closed beta, fixes, go/no-go by end of Q1.

sections.name: Risks
sections.guidance: Top risks, each with a likelihood and a concrete mitigation.
content: Sync conflicts may overwrite edits made on two devices. Likelihood: high. Mitigation: merge per field, keep both versions when a merge fails, and pass a conflict test suite before beta.
Storage limits on older phones. Likelihood: medium. Mitigation: cap the photo cache and warn the user before it fills.
Scope creep into tablet layouts. Likelihood: low. Mitigation: listed as a non-goal; Product lead rejects tablet tickets until after beta.

reviews.note: Sync conflicts are named as the top risk but there is no mitigation, and no risk has a mitigation at all. The brief says sync must never lose a note.
before: Sync conflicts may overwrite edits made on two devices. Likelihood: high.
Storage limits on older phones. Likelihood: medium.
Scope creep into tablet layouts. Likelihood: low.

sections.name: Dependencies
sections.guidance: Things that must happen or be decided first.
content: Choose the on-device database before the local storage work starts (the repo has no local store today).
Background sync permissions on iOS and Android.
The note ID format must become client-generated before offline creates can sync.

sections.name: Open questions
sections.guidance: Questions raised during the run that no agent could answer. Not reviewed.
content: Should conflicted notes show both versions to the user, or merge silently? (raised by Designer)
Do managed devices need admin controls over offline data? (raised by Researcher)
sources: Questions raised during the run that no agent could answer
